title: FORECAST - FOrecasting RElapse and Crisis in Acute Severe mental illness Trajectories Mixed-Methods-Machbarkeitsstudie eines digitalen Frühwarnsystems zur Prädiktion von psychischen Krisen bei Menschen mit schweren psychischen Erkrankungen
summary:
People with severe mental illness, including schizophrenia, bipolar, and depressive disorder, are at risk of relapse and mental health crises. Individuals often come into contact with healthcare services only once a crisis has already manifested. From a clinical perspective, there is a need to identify patients at increased risk at an early stage and enable timely intervention. 

The aim of the FORECAST study is to advance methods for the continuous prediction of mental health crises. A key innovation of our approach is to address gaps in routine data by incorporating prospectively collected Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs). This allows temporal fluctuations in patients’ trajectories to be integrated into crisis prediction. 

Our mixed-methods study comprises a quantitative part for the development of predictive models, preceded by a qualitative study involving focus groups and co-design workshops.  

The long-term goal is to develop a patient-centred approach for the early detection of mental health crises, with the potential to enable timely and preventive interventions.

interventions.name: Qualitative study component: Focus groups and co-design workshops involving healthcare professionals and patients from the Psychiatric Outpatient Departments (PIA) at Charité Campus Mitte (CCM) and St. Hedwig Hospital.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Retrospective Study / Replication Study: 
Routine clinical data from out- and inpatients, treated at the Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy at Charité Campus Mitte between 2019 and 2026. 

Prospective Study / PROM-Monitoring:
- Participants must be receiving outpatient psychiatric treatment. 
- Participants must have experienced ≥1 mental health crisis event (e.g., emergency department visit, psychiatric hospitalization, subjectively experienced crisis, or intensification of pharmacological treatment) within the past 12 months. 
- Participants must be able to communicate without the assistance of an interpreter. 
- Participants must have the capacity to provide informed consent and be at least 18 years of age. 
- Participants must have a diagnosis of schizophrenia (ICD-10: F20), schizoaffective disorder (ICD-10: F25), bipolar affective disorder (ICD-10: F31), depressive episode (ICD-10: F32), or recurrent depressive disorder (ICD-10: F33). 
- Participants must own an internet-enabled smartphone.
Exclusion criteria:
Prospective Study / PROM-Monitoring:
- Acute intoxication (ICD-10: F1x.0) or withdrawal syndrome (ICD-10: F1x.3) at the time of informed consent or data collection. 
- Inability to understand the content and implications of the study and to provide written informed consent. 
- Acute suicidality. 
- Organic mental disorders (ICD-10: F0x) and intellectual disability (ICD-10: F7x). 
- Substance dependence (ICD-10: F1x.2). 
- Acute risk of harm to self or others at the time of enrolment. 
- Physical health conditions or impairments that prevent regular participation and data entry via smartphone.
